caption: The Home card's guided-tour buttons: the new 'Connect two chiplets' tour sits below the three existing tours — the multi-chiplet story (rung 6) gets its guided entry point. Placement: own row under the tours, because all guided tours must be reachable from one glance at the Home card.

Tour step 1/6: the shipped Two-Chiplets example on the canvas — two dies joined by an edge-coupler link. The card anchors to the canvas. Placement: beside the design, because both dies and the link between them must stay visible.
Tour step 2/6: the toolbar's Run-simulation button is spotlighted. Placement: below the toolbar, so the card never covers the chiplets the user is about to simulate.

Tour step 3/6: the move step on the canvas, with the 'Move it for me' helper button that shifts the receiver die 5 µm through an undoable group move. Placement: beside the design, keeping both dies in view while the user drags.

Tour step 4/6: the receiver die sits 5 µm off its facet and the tour has opened the analysis dock on the Design Checks tab — the card points at Run checks. Placement: above the dock, so the tab and the canvas stay readable.

Tour step 5/6: the checker flags the facet gap and the card points at the 'Align chiplet' one-click fix next to Prev/Next. Placement: above the dock, keeping the finding row and the fix button uncovered.
Tour step 6/6: aligned again, checks clean — the closing card floats bottom-centre with the facet-gap takeaway and the pointer to the Gaussian-beam animation in the Design Checks help.
